As a Company, we possess three competitive advantages: 1) a broad and deep brand portfolio rooted in play; 2) one of the biggest and most diverse licensing businesses in the world and 3) a profitable games business anchored by MAGIC: THE GATHERING, DUNGEONS & DRAGONS, MONOPOLY, and Hasbro gaming classics.

competitive_position.claim: The play industry is described as highly competitive with low barriers to entry; new participants using digital media and social platforms (e.g., TikTok influencers) can rapidly gain consumer access and become significant competitors.

In addition to existing competitors, the barriers to entry for new participants in the play industry are low.

For example, with the use of influencers and media outlets such as Tik Tok, new participants with a popular product idea can gain access to consumers and become a significant source of competition for our products in a very short period of time.

competitive_position.claim: Consumer interests evolve quickly and can change dramatically year-to-year, creating short product life cycles and the risk of franchise fatigue from frequent releases or cross-brand collaborations.
quotes: Our ability to successfully create innovative products that inspire a lifetime of play is affected by the interests of children, families, fans and audiences which evolve quickly and can change dramatically from year to year and by geography.

Frequent product releases, cross-brand collaborations or expanded licensing initiatives may contribute to franchise fatigue or oversaturation, which could reduce long-term consumer engagement and diminish the value of our brands.

competitive_position.claim: Hasbro's reliance on third-party licenses (Marvel, Star Wars, Final Fantasy, Avatar, etc.) creates risk if licensed material has less market appeal than expected, minimum guaranteed royalties exceed actual sales, or licenses are not renewed.
quotes: We may not realize the full benefit of our licenses from third parties if the licensed material has less market appeal than expected, if revenue from the licensed products is not sufficient to earn out the minimum guaranteed royalties or if licenses are not renewed.

The license agreements we enter to obtain these rights usually require us to pay minimum royalty guarantees that may be substantial, and in some cases may be greater than what we are ultimately able to recoup from actual sales, which could result in write-offs and could harm our results of operations.
